criteria.text: The participant is ≥ 6 years old at the time of informed consent
The participant is ≥ 2 years to < 6 years old at the time of informed consent and may enroll onto PK cohort 1 if open, or onto phase 2 if PK cohort 1 is completed and deemed sufficient
The participant is ≥ 12 months to < 2 years old at the time of informed consent and may enroll onto PK cohort 2 if open, or onto phase 2 if PK cohort 2 is completed and deemed sufficient
The participant and/or their parents or legally authorized representatives sign a written informed consent, and assent is obtained when appropriate
The participant has a Karnofsky score ≥ 60% if > 16 years old, or a Lansky score ≥ 60 if ≤ 16 years old

The participant has Wilms tumor or nephroblastoma and meets at least one of the following: (1) in their second or greater relapse, (2) refractory or in their first relapse with high risk histology, or (3) refractory or in first relapse without high risk histology but after having received chemotherapies other than the initial 4 agents used as current standard of care in the up-front setting for non-high risk cases

The participant has a Rhabdoid tumor (including ATRT, MRTK, malignant rhabdoid tumors of the soft tissue and liver, SCUH, or SCCOHT) and has failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment
The participant has progressive, relapsed, unresectable or metastatic MPNST and has failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment

The participant does not qualify for Cohorts A, B, or C, has a solid tumor (no hematologic malignancies including lymphoma) for which there is specific evidence that this particular patient's tumor may benefit from selinexor, has failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment, and provides documentation of specific supporting evidence approved by the study principal investigator

The participant has a solid tumor with an activating genomic alteration involving BCOR (e.g., BCOR-ITD, BCOR-CCNB3, BCOR-MAML3, ZC3H7B-BCOR, or other potentially qualifying BCOR alterations approved by the study principal investigator), and does not have a loss of function alteration of BCOR
Patients on the phase II portion of the study have measurable disease, whereas patients on the PK cohorts have either evaluable or measurable disease as measured by RECIST 1.1

Patients with primary brain tumors have measurable disease for the phase II (or evaluable or measurable for the PK cohorts), defined as at least equal or greater than twice the slice thickness in two perpendicular diameters on MRI OR diffuse leptomeningeal disease OR clear MRI evidence of disease that may not be measurable in two perpendicular diameters OR positive CSF cytology alone

The participant has fully recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior anti-cancer therapy and meets minimum washout durations from prior therapy: ≥ 7 days for non-myelosuppressive agents, ≥ 21 days for myelosuppressive agents and immunotherapies, ≥ 42 days for adoptive cellular therapies and autologous stem cell transplantation, ≥ 84 days for allogeneic bone marrow transplantation, ≥ 14 days for focal external beam radiation, ≥ 42 days for substantial external beam radiation and radiopharmaceutical therapy
The participant has adequate hepatic function within 14 days prior to C1D1: total bilirubin < 1.5 × ULN (or < 3 × ULN for Gilbert's syndrome), ALT < 3 × ULN, and serum albumin ≥ 2 g/dL

The participant has adequate renal function within 14 days prior to C1D1, defined as a GFR ≥ 50 ml/min/1.73 m2 determined via nuclear radioisotope, 24 hr urine creatinine clearance, serum cystatin c, or serum creatinine using the Schwartz formula

The participant has adequate hematologic function within 14 days prior to C1D1: ANC ≥ 1000/mm3, platelet count ≥ 100,000/mm3, and has not received platelet transfusions or hematopoietic growth factor support for at least 7 days prior to demonstrating adequate function
The participant has received selinexor or another XPO1 inhibitor previously
The participant does not have an uncontrolled infection
The participant has not had a prior solid organ transplantation, and if they have received an allogeneic bone marrow transplant, they are not being actively treated for GvHD
The participant is able to comply with supportive care, safety monitoring, or any other key requirements of the study protocols
The participant is not pregnant or breast-feeding

Males or females of reproductive potential have agreed to use two effective methods of birth control, including a medically accepted barrier or contraceptive method, for the duration of the study, or practice abstinence

P1.text: Age ≥ 6 at the time of informed consent

P2.text: Age ≥ 2 years to \< 6 years at time of informed consent (Refer to Section 4.3): If PK cohort 1 is open, patients in this age range may enroll onto this cohort. If PK cohort 1 has been completed and deemed sufficient to proceed, then such patients may enroll onto the phase 2.

P3.text:
Age ≥ 12 months to \< 2 years at time of informed consent (Refer to Section 4.3):

If PK cohort 2 is open, patients in this age range may enroll onto this cohort. If PK cohort 2 has been completed and deemed sufficient to proceed, then such patients may enroll onto the phase 2.

P4.text: All patients and/or their parents or legally authorized representatives must sign a written informed consent. Assent, when appropriate, will be obtained according to institutional guidelines.

P5.text: Karnofsky ≥ 60% for patients \> 16 years of age and Lansky ≥ 60 for patients ≤ 16 years of age.

P6.text: Cohort A: Any type of Wilms tumor or nephroblastoma is eligible for this study provided they meet at least one of these criteria: (1) in their second or greater relapse, (2) refractory or in their first relapse with high risk histology (i.e., any anaplastic or blastemal-type after neoadjuvant chemotherapy), or (3) refractory or in first relapse without high risk histology but after having received chemotherapies other than the initial 4 agents used as current standard of care in the up-front setting for non-high risk cases - specifically vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin, and irinotecan (i.e., any patient who relapses following an initial regimen more intense than EE4A, DD4A, VAD, AVD, or VIVA; for example, those including cyclophosphamide/etoposide - such as Regimen I, M, or MVI - or those additionally including carboplatin - such as Regimens UH-1, UH-2, or UH-3).

P7.text: Cohort B: Any Rhabdoid tumor is eligible for this cohort. This includes, but is not limited to, related subtypes of rhabdoid tumors such as atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumors (ATRT), malignant rhabdoid tumors of the kidney (MRTK), malignant rhabdoid tumors of the soft tissue and liver, small cell undifferentiated hepatoblastomas (SCUH), and small-cell carcinoma of the ovary of hypercalcemic type (SCCOHT). Patients must have failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment.

P8.text: Cohort C: Patients with progressive, relapsed, unresectable or metastatic MPNST, are eligible for this cohort. Patients must have failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment.

P9.text:
Cohort D: Patients must not qualify for Cohorts A, B, or C but have a solid tumor (no hematologic malignancies including lymphoma) for which there is specific evidence that this particular patient's tumor may benefit from selinexor.

Patients must have failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment. Examples of evidence are listed below. All patients in this cohort require approval of study principal investigator and must provide documentation of specific supporting evidence. i. Tumor XPO1 Dependency: Defined as either Darwin OncoTarget demonstrating XPO1 as aberrantly activated or Darwin OncoTreat demonstrating context-specific tumor checkpoint inversion with Selinexor, both of which must be significant at a -log10 (Bonferroni corrected p-value) of 5 or greater. ii. Tumor XPO1 Activation: Defined as the detection of a gain of function mutation in XPO1, specifically E571K. Additionally, detection of elevated transcriptomic or proteomic expression of XPO1 in the tumor via RNAseq or IHC, respectively, would be considered sufficient for treatment.

iii. Preclinical Tumor Testing: Defined as testing of Selinexor on patient derived cell line, organoid, or xenograft models of the patient's tumor (or other related tumors) performed in a laboratory context and for which, in the investigator's opinion, demonstrates promising activity. Testing may include commercial testing as well as academic laboratory testing.

P10.text: Cohort E: Patients must have a solid tumor with an activating genomic alteration (e.g. fusion or internal tandem duplication) involving BCOR. Specific examples of qualifying alterations including BCOR-ITD, BCOR-CCNB3, BCOR-MAML3 and ZC3H7B-BCOR; Other potentially qualifying BCOR alterations require approval of study principal investigator; note that loss of function alterations of BCOR would not qualify.

P11.text: Patients on the phase II portion of the study must have measurable disease whereas patients on the PK cohorts can have either evaluable or measurable disease as measured by the revised Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) guideline (Version 1.1).

P12.text: Primary Brain Tumors: Patients with primary brain tumors are eligible and must also have measurable disease for the phase II (as well as evaluable or measurable for the PK cohorts), but this can be defined as at least equal or greater than twice the slice thickness in two perpendicular diameters on MRI OR diffuse leptomeningeal disease OR clear MRI evidence of disease that may not be measurable in two perpendicular diameters OR positive CSF cytology alone.

P13.text:
Patients must have fully recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior anti-cancer therapy and meet minimum washout durations (shown below) from prior therapy.

  1. Anti-cancer agents not known to be myelosuppressive: ≥ 7 days
  2. Anti-cancer and cytotoxic agents known to be myelosuppressive: ≥ 21 days
  3. Immunotherapies (including antibodies, interleukins, interferons, etc.): ≥ 21 days
  4. Adoptive cellular therapies (including modified T cells, vaccines, etc.): ≥ 42 days
  5. Autologous stem cell infusion (boost, no conditioning): ≥ 21 days
  6. Autologous stem cell transplantation (with conditioning): ≥ 42 days
  7. Allogeneic bone marrow transplantation: ≥ 84 days
  8. Focal external beam radiation (e.g., limited sites of disease): ≥ 14 days
  9. Substantial external beam radiation (e.g. whole lung or abdomen): ≥ 42 days
  10. Radiopharmaceutical therapy (e.g., radiolabeled antibody or MIBG): ≥ 42 days

P14.text:
Hepatic Function: Adequate function (within 14 days prior to C1D1), defined as:

  1. Total bilirubin \< 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN) (except patients with Gilbert's syndrome, who must have a total bilirubin of \<3 × ULN)
  2. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) \< 3 × ULN
  3. Serum albumin ≥ 2 g/dL

P15.text:
Renal Function: Adequate function (within 14 days prior to C1D1) defined as a GFR

  ≥ 50 ml/min/1.73 m2 determined via any of these methods:
  1. Nuclear radioisotope
  2. 24 hr urine creatinine clearance
  3. Serum cystatin c
  4. Serum creatinine using the Schwartz formula for estimating creatinine clearance (Schwartz et al. J Peds, 106:522, 1985)

P16.text:
Hematologic Function: Adequate function (within 14 days prior to C1D1), defined as:

  1. Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1000/mm3
  2. Platelet count ≥ 100,000/mm3
  3. Note: patients may not receive platelet transfusions nor hematopoietic growth factor support, including granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (e.g. filgrastim) and platelet stimulators (e.g. romiplostim) for at least 7 days prior to demonstrating adequate hematologic function.

P17.text: Prior Therapy: Has received selinexor or another XPO1 inhibitor previously.

P18.text: Infection: Patients who have an uncontrolled infection are not eligible. Patients on prophylactic antibiotics or with a controlled infection within 1 week prior to C1D1 are acceptable

P19.text: Transplants: Patients who have received allogeneic bone marrow transplant are potentially eligible unless they are being actively treated for GvHD. Patients who have had a prior solid organ transplantation are not eligible.

P20.text: Compliance: Patients who as a result of serious medical, psychiatric, and/or social situation(s), in the opinion of the investigator, may not be able to comply with supportive care, safety monitoring, or any other key requirements of the study protocols are not eligible.

P21.text: Pregnancy and Breast-feeding: Pregnant or breast-feeding women will not be entered on this study because there is yet no available information regarding human fetal or teratogenic toxicities. Pregnancy tests must be obtained in girls who are post-menarchal.

P22.text: Contraception: Males or females of reproductive potential may not participate unless they have agreed to use two effective methods of birth control, including a medically accepted barrier or contraceptive method (e.g., male or female condom) for the duration of the study. Abstinence is an acceptable method of birth control.

transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study of Selinexor in People With Wilms Tumors and Other Solid Tumors". Your earlier answers already covered 5 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, are you 6 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm 73.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. This study is for participants aged 2 to under 6 years. Since you are 73, would you like to skip this question?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, please skip it. I'm way too old for this one.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Would you be willing to sign a written informed consent form to participate in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: My son helps me with the paperwork. I think so, but I'll need his help to read it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, are you willing to sign the consent form yourself, with your son's help if needed?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I can sign it. My son helps me with the paperwork, so I'll be fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know your Karnofsky or Lansky score, which measures daily functioning? If not, that's okay—just let me know if you're unsure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what that score is. I'm up most of the day but can't work at all.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Has your son's Wilms tumor relapsed, or is it still present despite treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have a child with Wilms tumor. I'm 73 and retired.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with a rhabdoid tumor (such as ATRT or malignant rhabdoid tumor)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have that. I have non-small cell lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you tried at least one systemic therapy (like chemotherapy or immunotherapy) for your lung cancer that did not work?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No treatment yet. They only just found it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any genetic or genomic testing done on your lung cancer tumor to check for changes in the BCOR gene?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Don't know. My son might know about the specific genes they tested, but I don't.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you have lung cancer, does this study criterion about primary brain tumors apply to you at all?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have a primary brain tumor. The cancer spread to my brain from my lungs, but it started in my chest.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any cancer treatments (like chemo, immunotherapy, or radiation) in the last 12 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No. They only just found it, so I haven't had any treatments yet.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any uncontrolled infections, such as a serious bacterial, viral, or fungal infection?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any uncontrolled infections right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to follow the study's schedule for visits, tests, and other requirements?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm tired and it's hard, but my son helps me with things. I think I can manage the visits with his help.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, are you able to follow the study's schedule for visits, tests, and other requirements, including any supportive care or safety monitoring?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I think so. My son helps me with things, so I should be able to manage the visits and tests.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently using two effective methods of birth control (such as a barrier method plus another contraceptive) or practicing abstinence?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I'm 73 and retired. I don't need birth control.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.

rule.registry:
Hepatic Function: Adequate function (within 14 days prior to C1D1), defined as:

  1. Total bilirubin \< 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN) (except patients with Gilbert's syndrome, who must have a total bilirubin of \<3 × ULN)
  2. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) \< 3 × ULN
  3. Serum albumin ≥ 2 g/dL

rule.registry:
Renal Function: Adequate function (within 14 days prior to C1D1) defined as a GFR

  ≥ 50 ml/min/1.73 m2 determined via any of these methods:
  1. Nuclear radioisotope
  2. 24 hr urine creatinine clearance
  3. Serum cystatin c
  4. Serum creatinine using the Schwartz formula for estimating creatinine clearance (Schwartz et al. J Peds, 106:522, 1985)

why.ours: A lab value: your records will have it.

rule.registry:
Hematologic Function: Adequate function (within 14 days prior to C1D1), defined as:

  1. Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1000/mm3
  2. Platelet count ≥ 100,000/mm3
  3. Note: patients may not receive platelet transfusions nor hematopoietic growth factor support, including granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (e.g. filgrastim) and platelet stimulators (e.g. romiplostim) for at least 7 days prior to demonstrating adequate hematologic function.

rule.registry: Cohort A: Any type of Wilms tumor or nephroblastoma is eligible for this study provided they meet at least one of these criteria: (1) in their second or greater relapse, (2) refractory or in their first relapse with high risk histology (i.e., any anaplastic or blastemal-type after neoadjuvant chemotherapy), or (3) refractory or in first relapse without high risk histology but after having received chemotherapies other than the initial 4 agents used as current standard of care in the up-front setting for non-high risk cases - specifically vincristine, dactinomycin, doxorubicin, and irinotecan (i.e., any patient who relapses following an initial regimen more intense than EE4A, DD4A, VAD, AVD, or VIVA; for example, those including cyclophosphamide/etoposide - such as Regimen I, M, or MVI - or those additionally including carboplatin - such as Regimens UH-1, UH-2, or UH-3).

rule.registry: Cohort B: Any Rhabdoid tumor is eligible for this cohort. This includes, but is not limited to, related subtypes of rhabdoid tumors such as atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumors (ATRT), malignant rhabdoid tumors of the kidney (MRTK), malignant rhabdoid tumors of the soft tissue and liver, small cell undifferentiated hepatoblastomas (SCUH), and small-cell carcinoma of the ovary of hypercalcemic type (SCCOHT). Patients must have failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment.

rule.registry:
Cohort D: Patients must not qualify for Cohorts A, B, or C but have a solid tumor (no hematologic malignancies including lymphoma) for which there is specific evidence that this particular patient's tumor may benefit from selinexor.

Patients must have failed to respond to at least 1 line of systemic therapy prior to enrollment. Examples of evidence are listed below. All patients in this cohort require approval of study principal investigator and must provide documentation of specific supporting evidence. i. Tumor XPO1 Dependency: Defined as either Darwin OncoTarget demonstrating XPO1 as aberrantly activated or Darwin OncoTreat demonstrating context-specific tumor checkpoint inversion with Selinexor, both of which must be significant at a -log10 (Bonferroni corrected p-value) of 5 or greater. ii. Tumor XPO1 Activation: Defined as the detection of a gain of function mutation in XPO1, specifically E571K. Additionally, detection of elevated transcriptomic or proteomic expression of XPO1 in the tumor via RNAseq or IHC, respectively, would be considered sufficient for treatment.

iii. Preclinical Tumor Testing: Defined as testing of Selinexor on patient derived cell line, organoid, or xenograft models of the patient's tumor (or other related tumors) performed in a laboratory context and for which, in the investigator's opinion, demonstrates promising activity. Testing may include commercial testing as well as academic laboratory testing.
